groups.title: Several computers (with the sync engine, config-sync)

parts.name: team
parts.what: Base rules given to Claude every session (added to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md by install.sh): Claude works as a teammate, challenges you, and asks before production, commits, pushes, PRs and decisions that need your context.
parts.why: Claude stops taking risky steps on its own and stops agreeing just to please.
parts.who: Anyone.

parts.name: statusline
parts.what: A status line with folder, branch, model, context used, effort and rate limit.
parts.why: You see when the context fills up or a limit comes, before it bites.
parts.who: Anyone.

parts.name: file-tools-guard
parts.what: Blocks shell workarounds (cat, sed -i, heredocs) for reading and editing files.
parts.why: Claude's own file tools show clickable line numbers and fail loudly instead of mangling a file.
parts.when: Each time Claude runs a shell command.
parts.who: Anyone.

parts.name: recent-prompts
parts.what: Your last two messages above the prompt, and a searchable history pane.
parts.why: You find again what you asked without scrolling a long session.
parts.who: Anyone.

parts.name: dnd
parts.what: Do-not-disturb profiles for the history, PR & CI and reminders-handoffs panes: hide a pane, or keep only some repos, reminder groups or the session's own repo.
parts.why: At the office, in a meeting or in one repo, the panes show only what matters there, by themselves.
parts.when: Turned on by hand (the Configuration button, /dnd, or ask Claude), or by a rule: a Wi-Fi network, days and hours, a folder.
parts.who: Anyone with one of those panes.

parts.name: paste-preview
parts.what: Pasted text shown in full, and previews of pasted images.
parts.why: You check what you pasted before sending it.
parts.who: macOS and Windows.

parts.name: recent-activity
parts.what: A digest of your recent sessions across your dev folder, at session start.
parts.why: Claude knows what you did lately in your other repos when you mention them.
parts.who: Anyone with several repos in one folder.

parts.name: session-registry
parts.what: Offers to resume the session left open in a terminal tab.
parts.why: A closed tab or a reboot no longer loses the session you were in.
parts.who: zsh users (JetBrains or Ghostty terminals).

parts.name: wave-check
parts.what: A self-check whenever a reply doesn't start with your marker emoji.
parts.why: A missing emoji is the first sign Claude stopped following your CLAUDE.md; the check makes it fix that.
parts.who: Anyone; pick this or wave-check-hook.

parts.name: wave-check-hook
parts.what: A warning whenever a reply doesn't start with your marker emoji (the hook form of wave-check).
parts.why: Same as wave-check, for setups without mods.
parts.who: Anyone who doesn't load mods.

parts.name: nocturne-notify
parts.what: Keyboard-backlight signals of Claude's state through Agent Nocturne (github.com/taekchef/agent-nocturne).
parts.why: You see from across the room when Claude waits for you.
parts.who: Agent Nocturne users.

parts.name: git-identity-guard
parts.what: Refuses a commit or push whose email isn't the one you chose for that host (GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, any), or, with no rule, the one you used most in that repo. Can also check every commit and push made outside Claude.
parts.why: One work email on a personal or public repo can expose your employer, or make a security team think secrets leaked.
parts.who: Anyone committing with different emails (work, personal, clients), even on a single host.

parts.name: pr-watch
parts.what: Tracks your PRs until merged: new comments, votes, CI results, merges; your own PRs and review requests too.
parts.why: You know when a PR needs you without refreshing pages.
parts.when: Each session start, and when you ask.
parts.who: GitHub (gh) or Azure DevOps (az or a PAT) users.

parts.name: pr-pane
parts.what: A /prs pane of the PRs pr-watch tracks: status, CI, what each waits for, open in the browser, live refresh.
parts.why: All your PRs at a glance, colored by what you have to do.
parts.when: The PRs button above the prompt, or /prs.
parts.who: pr-watch users.

parts.name: test-evidence
parts.what: Screenshots, a short video and network proof of a ticket tested locally, attached to Jira or the PR.
parts.why: A reviewer trusts what they can see working.
parts.when: After testing a change: "take screenshots", "proof for the PR".
parts.who: Web developers (needs the chrome-devtools MCP; video needs ffmpeg).

parts.name: ci-review
parts.what: An AI review step on CI that checks each PR/MR against its proof (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI).
parts.why: Nobody reviews a PR by hand just to check that it works.
parts.when: Once per repo: "set up AI review on CI".
parts.who: Teams with CI and an API key or a cloud provider.

parts.name: capability-builder
parts.what: Turns a request you keep making into a skill, hook or mod: picks the right kind, scaffolds it with tests, checks it on macOS, Linux and Windows, and runs the publish checklist.
parts.why: A capability that works everywhere and others can use, instead of a one-off prompt.
parts.when: "Make this a skill", or when Claude notices you asking the same thing again.
parts.who: Anyone who wants to build their own, or contribute to this kit.

parts.name: learn
parts.what: Claude ends a reply with a short, precise lesson when the work touches security, an architecture choice, a design pattern or a performance trap, quoting the real code. /learn off, brief, normal or deep per session; the status line shows 💡 and the level, and the history pane lists the lessons.
parts.why: You learn the why behind the code while you work, without asking for it every time.
parts.when: At the end of a reply, only when there is something worth learning.
parts.who: Anyone who wants to learn from the work; pair it with statusline and recent-prompts.

parts.name: kb
parts.what: A personal knowledge base: Markdown notes with [[links]] in your config sync (or ~/.claude/knowledge), indexed in SQLite for text, semantic (a local multilingual model) and graph search. Every morning, Claude reads the previous day's transcripts of this computer and proposes notes, written with a report. The notes that match the repository, the branch or the prompt are recalled at session start and on each prompt; a server (and a container) gives them to your other agents.
parts.why: What you decided and learned in a session is found again later, on every computer, instead of being asked again or lost in old transcripts.
parts.when: Each session start and prompt; every morning for the curation; "what do you know about…", "note this for good".
parts.who: Anyone with Python 3.12 (the morning curation needs daily-sync and the Claude Code CLI signed in).

parts.name: config-sync
parts.what: The sync engine: keeps your CLAUDE.md, skills, mods, hooks, plugins and their settings, MCP servers (secrets left out) and memory the same on all your computers, through a private git repo of your own (any host; created for you on GitHub with gh if you like).
parts.why: Set Claude up once, and every computer works the same way, with the same plugins and memory.
parts.when: In the background at each session start, after each reply and at session end.
parts.who: People who use Claude Code on two computers or more; handoff, daily-sync and reminders need it.

parts.name: handoff
parts.what: Handoff notes between computers.
parts.why: You continue on the other computer without explaining everything again.
parts.who: People working on two computers or more.

parts.name: daily-sync
parts.what: Syncs before the first session of the day and every morning at a time you pick.
parts.why: Each computer starts the day with what the others left.
parts.who: Sync engine users.

parts.name: reminders
parts.what: Reminders for a later session, notified on the desktop and the phone every morning.
parts.why: What you mean to do tomorrow, or on the other computer, doesn't get lost.
parts.who: Sync engine users.

parts.name: reminders-handoffs
parts.what: One pane for your reminders (due now, upcoming and repeating, past) and your handoff notes (open, done), a tab each, filed by group, with done, stop, pick, cancel and delete.
parts.why: What you left for later, on any computer, at a glance, and one click to close it or pick it up.
parts.when: The button above the prompt, /reminders-pane or /handoffs-pane.
parts.who: People who use reminders, handoff or both: it shows whichever is installed.

parts.name: video-montage
parts.what: Video montages from a folder of phone clips, an Instagram Reel by default.
parts.why: A finished reel from raw clips without an editing app.
parts.who: Anyone with ffmpeg (saving to Photos needs macOS).

parts.name: insta360-montage
parts.what: Video montages from raw Insta360 footage, an Instagram Reel by default.
parts.why: The best moments of a session found and cut without Insta360 Studio.
parts.who: Insta360 X-series owners.
